instruction: Add both open tabs to the bookmarks bar.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully bookmarked the active tab (Illustrated Transformer) to bookmarks bar using Ctrl+D, changed folder to Bookmarks bar, and toggled bar visibility with Ctrl+Shift+B. Completed in 6 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can switch tabs, use Ctrl+D to bookmark, select bookmark folder, toggle bookmarks bar visibility
metadata.task_rationale: Harder variation requiring bookmarking both tabs instead of just one, testing repeated bookmark workflow and tab switching
metadata.explanation: Task requires bookmarking both open tabs to the bookmarks bar. Evaluator restarts Chrome and checks bookmarks bar contains both URLs. Uses the standard is_expected_bookmarks metric which checks all provided URLs exist in bookmarks bar.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_bookmarks) correctly reads Chrome's Bookmarks JSON file from disk, returning the roots dict with bookmark_bar structure.
Postconfig correctly kills and restarts Chrome to ensure bookmarks are flushed to disk before reading.
Expected values (get_rule) correctly pass the rules dict directly to the metric, matching the two URLs from the opened tabs.
Metric (is_expected_bookmarks) correctly handles 'bookmark_bar_websites_urls' type by extracting URLs from bookmark_bar children.
Full instruction coverage: both URLs from the two open tabs are verified in the bookmarks bar.

Minor concern: metric uses strict set equality (==) instead of superset check (>=), so pre-existing bookmarks in the bar would cause a false negative. Acceptable if the snapshot starts with an empty bookmarks bar.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using set(rule['urls']).issubset(set(bookmark_bar_websites_urls)) instead of strict set equality, to be robust against pre-existing bookmarks in the bar.
